verdict.rationale: Both suites are correct; every expected value I checked by hand matches the code, and both leave src/rates.ts untouched. They cover nearly the same ground, with tie cases that tell half-up from half-even, fee boundaries, error paths and quote coverage. A's report is accurate (35 new + 10 existing = 45). B's report gives the wrong breakdown: it claims 31 new + 8 existing, when it actually has 29 new + 10 existing. That tips it slightly toward A, although B follows the repo's flat `test()` style more closely.

The 'net plus fee always equals converted' test is close to a tautology given how quote computes net
Report says expected values were taken from the code's current behavior rather than derived independently
b_issues: Report misstates the test counts: 29 new tests plus 10 existing, not 31 plus 8 (the total of 39 is right)
Checks minorUnitsOf for only three of the five currencies

verdict.rationale: I checked every expected value in both suites against the rate table and `divideRounded`, and all of them are correct. Both suites are thorough characterization tests and leave `src/rates.ts` untouched. A is slightly sharper. It picks tie cases where half-up and half-even give different results for the same currency pair (15 EUR cents to USD gives 17, where half-even would give 16). It also probes just below the minimum-fee boundary (1199 EUR, fee 29.975) and keeps the repo's flat `test()` style. B's report says its expected values were taken from the code's current behavior, which is weaker as an independent safety net, though it also says the tie cases were hand-computed.
a_issues: Report says 31 new tests plus 8 existing. The diff has 29 new tests and the repo has 10 existing ones; the total of 39 is still right.
b_issues: Report says expected values were taken from the code's current behavior, which conflicts with its claim that the tie cases were hand-computed.
The `net + fee === converted` loop is close to tautological, since `quote` computes `net` as `converted - fee`.
Uses `describe` blocks, while the existing test files use flat `test()` calls.
A comment in the JPY case reads "16.25 * 10 = 1625", which is muddled arithmetic even though the assertion is correct.
